newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Arafat tells U.N. council Israel harms peace process.
newsitem.headline: Arafat tells U.N. council Israel harms peace process.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat told Security Council members on Wednesday that Israel was harming the Middle East peace process by planning a new Jewish neighbourhood on the southern edge of East Jerusalem, captured during the 1967 Middle East war.

He was speaking to reporters after conferring privately with the members of the 15-nation council a few hours before the start of a council debate on Israel's plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a tree-covered hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem, one of the towns now under Palestinian self-rule.
The building site is called Har Homa by Israel and Jebel Abu Ghneim by the Palestinians.
Arafat said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was "pushing the peace process in very critical and crucial circumstances."
"They are saying it is Har Homa settlement. The target is to replace Har Homa instead of Bethlehem and to separate Jerusalem from Bethlehem," he said.
Israel regards the entire city of Jerusalem as its undivided capital while the Palestinians see East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state.

"My message today is how to implement accurately and honestly what had been agreed upon, to prevent any provocations and breaching (of) the United Nations and Security Council resolutions, which is the platform of the peace process," Arafat said.

"We went to Madrid according to resolutions 242 and 338 and land for peace. This is what we are asking," he added, referring to the 1991 conference that launched the peace process and U.N. resolutions adopted in 1967 and 1973 that embodied the idea of land for peace.
Asked what message he had for Netanyahu, Arafat said: "To coordinate together, to implement accurately and honestly what has been agreed on."

In similar remarks after conferring with Secretary-General Kofi Annan, Arafat said the new Israeli settlement was an issue not only for the Palestinians but also "for the Arabs, for the Moslems, for the Christians."
Several council members who attended the meeting with Arafat characterised his tone as moderate.

They said the thrust of his remarks was that the United Nations had supported the Middle East peace process throughout and that the latest Israeli action was a violation of peace commitments as well as of various Security Council resolutions. He also stressed that the United Nations continued to have a role in keeping the peace process on track.

Before visiting the United Nations, Arafat met 11 American Jewish leaders and said 29 paragraphs of the Palestinian Covenant calling for the elimination of Israel had been annulled, according to a spokesman for the group, Howard Squadron.
Revision of the Covenant was one of the conditions under which Israel agreed to withdraw from parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
"He said publicly that the offensive paragraphs are not there and have been annulled and that a Palestinian legal committee was working on a revised charter," Squadron said.
